title: Unstick a delayed US visa
summary: You cannot force a stuck visa, only push. First find where it is stuck: CEAC for the consulate, the USCIS case tracker for the petition. With 221(g) administrative processing, know what you are in: no fixed timeline, no appeal. Most cases resolve; some take months. Your moves: a documented expedite request against USCIS's published criteria, Form I-907 premium processing if your petition type qualifies (law rule us-fed.premium-processing-timeframe: USCIS must approve, deny, issue a notice of intent to deny, or request evidence within 15 business days for the designated I-129 classes, or refund the fee; it does nothing for a consular 221(g)), immigration counsel, and a congressional inquiry with your signed privacy release. Plan B: run the company remotely while you wait. Educational guidance, not legal advice. CEAC and the USCIS tracker sit behind bot walls, so status checks are done by hand, not API.

execution.rationale: Draft an evidence-linked expedite argument against the published criteria for counsel and applicant review.

parts.title: File Form I-907 premium processing if your petition classification qualifies (designated I-129/I-140 classes per USCIS)

execution.rationale: Eligibility, filer authorization and the accepted premium-processing submission route require the actual petition facts.

parts.title: Engage immigration counsel on the 221(g) response and the escalation paths

execution.rationale: Immigration counsel determines case-specific escalation from the notices; the engagement channel is unspecified.

parts.title: Sign the privacy release and open a congressional inquiry through your district office

execution.rationale: The constituent personally signs the district office's privacy release; the actual office's execution route is unspecified.

parts.title: Set the honest plan B: run the company remotely from your current country until the visa clears

execution.rationale: The founder decides and carries out the temporary remote operating plan while awaiting immigration action.

parts.title: Wait for consular or USCIS action, re-checking status weekly

execution.rationale: The weekly work is checking the CEAC and USCIS status pages already named in this process. Both provide case-status lookups; personal case details and CEAC's image-code challenge require the authorized person's handoff. The agencies retain the case decision.

metadata.trigger: Your US visa is stuck (221(g) administrative processing after the interview, or a petition sitting past posted times) while the company needs you in Silicon Valley.
metadata.supportReason: The status portals are captcha-gated government surfaces, the 221(g) response and expedite case are judgment calls made with counsel, and a congressional inquiry moves only on your signed privacy release. An agent can draft the expedite memo from your records; it cannot move a consulate.
